premises.text: Microsatellite ride-share launches force compromises on schedule, destination orbit, and integration, adding up to ~2.5 years before satellites are operational while capital burns
premises.evidence_span: Adding up all these pain points can lead to two and a half years between when a launch is scheduled and when a satellite is operational

premises.text: Reusable autonomous high-altitude balloon platform Regulus launches a smaller dedicated solid/liquid rocket from 60,000 feet, enabling weeks-to-orbit dedicated microsatellite launches to any LEO at high frequency
premises.evidence_span: Regulus is a fully reusable and autonomous vehicle that allows us to launch rockets from 60,000 feet in altitude

value.text: Dedicated microsatellite launch when and where customers need, without ride-share compromise
value.evidence_span: providing our microsatellite customers with a dedicated launch service that they've been asking for

secondary_value.text: High-altitude platform services market beyond orbital launch
secondary_value.evidence_span: this opens the door to a $2.6 billion high-altitude platform services market

causal_links.evidence_span: what customers need is the experience that you and I know is ride-sharing, where you can call up a ride that takes you where you want to go, when you want to get there, no compromise
Leo Aerospace can provide a launch within a matter of weeks to any low-Earth orbit and support a very high launch frequency

notes: Preset schedules/orbit drop-off/integration restrictions folded as one ride-share pain-bundle (rule 6). Balloon ascent, rotational control, solid stages, liquid third stage, and autonomous recovery folded as feature cascade of Regulus dedicated-launch mechanism (rule 7). NASA/Air Force/HAPS uses treated as applications of same platform, not extra premises.
